subject: Help in loop in dfreq() function

messages.author: fe1cd1573520a129
messages.subject: Help in loop in dfreq() function
parts:
Hi all,
I am trying to write a script for measuring temporal parameters in a frog call and then, based on the temporal 
measurements (begin and final time for each frog call) measure the dominant frequency in 10 different signal
parts. I made a loop for measuring the dominant frequency, but the "spec_param" table shows only the last
iteration (first with time position in the first column and frequency in the second an then the other way) until
the end of the matrix. Is my loop ok? Does someone could help? This is the code:
som<-readWave("call.wav")
png("temp_param.png", point=12, width=4000, height=3000, res=300)
temp_param<-timer(som,f=44100,threshold=20,dmin=0.015,msmooth=c(50,0))
dev.off()
cantos<-matrix(nrow=(length(temp_param$s)),ncol=2)
cantos[,1]<-temp_param$s.start
cantos[,2]<-temp_param$s.end
show(cantos)
spec_param<-matrix(nrow=(12*(length(temp_param$s))),ncol=2)
for (i in (length(temp_param$s))){
   spec_param[,]<-dfreq(som,f=44100,threshold=20,at=seq((cantos[i,1]),
    (cantos[i,2]),length.out=10),plot=FALSE)  
}
Thank you very much!

Me. Pedro P. G. Taucce

Universidade Estadual Paulista "Júlio de Mesquita Filho" - UNESP

messages.author: d91178de15999ecf
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Help in loop in dfreq() function
parts:
Hi Pedro,

There are two immediate problem I see is with the code:

1) for (i in (length(temp_param$s)))
This only iterates over one value: the length of temp_param$s
I think you mean:
  for(i in 1:length(temp_param$s))
Which iterates over 1 through the length of temp_param$s

2) spec_param[,] <- dfreq(...)
As far as I know, this tells R to save the output of dfreq as an object called spec_param. Although you specify [,] this doesn't actually mean anything, so this is why spec_param only has the last iteration saved.

I'm also confused as to what you hope to get in the end... your matrix is 12 x the length of temp_param$s, but you're only taking 10 dfreq samples, right? Also, why only have only two columns in your matrix, as opposed to the number of calls in your wave file (length(temp_param$s))?


As it looks as if you are taking 10 dfreq measurements at different spots in "call.wav", I would suggest using a data frame:

spec_param <- expand.grid(wave_file = "call.wav", call = temp_param$s, sample = 1:10,  dfreq = NA)
for (i in 1:length(temp_param$s)) {
  spec_param$dfreq[spec_param$call == temp_param$s[i]] <- dfreq(...)
}

Let me know if this helps!

Steffi

Dr. Stefanie LaZerte
Post-Doctoral Researcher
Natural Resources and Environmental Studies
University of Northern BC
stefanie...@unbc.ca
http://steffi.ca/

parts: Hi Steffi, thanks for your answer!

1) for (i in (length(temp_param$s))) 
This only iterates over one value: the length of temp_param$s
I think you mean:
  for(i in 1:length(temp_param$s))
Which iterates over 1 through the length of temp_param$s
Yes, thank you!

2) spec_param[,] <- dfreq(...)
As far as I know, this tells R to save the output of dfreq as an object called spec_param. Although you specify [,] this doesn't actually mean anything, so this is why spec_param only has the last iteration saved.
I'm also confused as to what you hope to get in the end... your matrix is 12 x the length of temp_param$s, but you're only taking 10 dfreq samples, right? Also, why only have only two columns in your matrix, as opposed to the number of calls in your wave file (length(temp_param$s))?
I was only taking ten measurements, but I don't know why, when I was doing it without the loop, dfreq() always returned the frequency at 0 time and at the end of the call. That is why the 12.
As it looks as if you are taking 10 dfreq measurements at different spots in "call.wav", I would suggest using a data frame:

for (i in 1:length(temp_param$s)) {
  spec_param$dfreq[spec_param$call == temp_param$s[i]] <- dfreq(...)
}
spec_param <- expand.grid(wave_file = "call.wav", call = temp_param$s, sample = 1:10,  dfreq = NA)

The data frame is in a much more useful and elegant way then I first thought it was possible, so thank you!

But it didn't work the way it is. I will try to explain exactly what I was thinking:

The timer function gives a list of six vectors, but for the loop I am interested in two:

s.start - start position of signal period 
s.end - end position of signal period

In order to measure only signals which I already know the calls are. So I thougth making a table with each s.start and s.end pairs in a line, representing the frog calls I have throughout the .wav file:

cantos<-matrix(nrow=(length(temp_param$s)),ncol=2)
cantos[,1]<-temp_param$s.start
cantos[,2]<-temp_param$s.end

And then I could use each position on a loop to measure all the signals in ten spots of each signal:
"at=seq((cantos[i,1]),(cantos[i,2]),length.out=10)"
I wish now I have helped you to help me. Does it also help if | send you the .wav file?
Thank you very much!

Pedro

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Help in loop in dfreq() function
parts:
Hi Pedro,

Well if dfreq is giving you 12 measures, you'll want to change the code somewhat (because with only 10 spots in the data frame, if you try to insert 12 items the code will probably result in a warning). Also, it might be nice to have a record of exactly where the dfreq measure is being taken. If you're SURE that the dfreq measures you want are only the middle 10, then the following code should get you what you're looking for (note the added [2:11] at the end). But I would double check the output of dfreq, as it seems a bit odd.

And yes, if this doesn't work, send me your call.wav file and I'll see what I can do!

spec_param <- expand.grid(wave_file = "call.wav", call = temp_param$s, sample = 1:12,  time = NA, dfreq = NA)
for (i in 1:length(temp_param$s)) {

spec_param$time[spec_param$call == temp_param$s[i]] <- seq((cantos[i, 1]),(cantos[i, 2]), length.out = 10)
    spec_param$dfreq[spec_param$call == temp_param$s[i]] <- dfreq(som, f = 44100, threshold = 20, at = seq((cantos[i, 1]), (cantos[i, 2]), length.out = 10), plot = FALSE)[2:11]
}

Enjoy,

Steffi
Dr. Stefanie LaZerte
Post-Doctoral Researcher
Natural Resources and Environmental Studies
University of Northern BC
stefanie...@unbc.ca
http://steffi.ca/

Hi Pedro,

I forgot how dfreq works, and you're right, the fact that it produces two columns is part of the problem. I've attached an annotated script showing you two alternative ways of constructing your loop. I've also changed a couple of other things in your script:

1) I've added spaces around = and <- and after , In general it easier to read a script if it's spaced out, but ultimately it's a matter of preference.
2) I've changed your cantos matrix to a cantos data frame. I think matrices might be computationally faster, but I find data frames easier to deal with and more intuitive, so for script clarity, I generally prefer to deal with data frames. And I changed the column names so they're more intuitive.
3) I've removed extra ( ). You only need () to group mathematical/logical operations or to define function arguments.

As you can probably, tell, none of these changes are bout turning "wrong" code into "right" code. In R you can achieve the same goal through many many different ways. I've merely put things in my style, because I find it a bit easier to follow and read, see if it works for you, if not, put it back to what you prefer!
